children.text: Input-card faces carrying the two live conditioning signals. #697 slice S5, frame 2 of 3. CLIP is the input overload badge (from le_snapshot.input_clip_mask): a filled record-red alarm — a rail run of >=4 samples at >=0.999 held ~1.5 s. It reads the RAW ADC, upstream of the HPF/notch, which is why it can light on the guitar card even though that input is being conditioned: the converter clips before any biquad can act, so conditioning must never suppress it. The input's own peak meter turns its top/peak segment record-red at the same moment, so the meter itself signals clip — not just the badge. Filled red (not the outline of MODIFIED) marks it as an alarm, not a status. Owner decision 2026-08-27: clip is INPUT-ONLY — a property of the physical jack (raw ADC), never the track; the track-face clip treatment (the former 'STAGE / track-hot' frame) is dropped, and the user-facing word is CLIP, not HOT. Engine state is unchanged: a_input_clip_mask / LE_CLIP_* internally; only the label reads CLIP. The COND line (from input_cond_mask) names the active sections — HPF · HUM · EXP — in accent when on, muted 'COND · OFF' when the stage is bypassed; it sits below the existing MONITOR line because both are facts about the jack. CLIP (red) / MODIFIED (amber outline, chain drift) / COND (accent) stay three distinct colours so a glance separates 'the input is overloading' from 'the chain drifted from its rack' from 'the input is being cleaned up'.
